heading: Public methods coordinate
body:
A service or a controller has two kinds of methods. A public method is an entry point: a page, a route or another class calls it. A private method is a helper that only its own class calls. Tachyon asks each kind of method to do one job.

A public method only coordinates. It calls injected services and private methods, it stores or returns their results, and it builds models and values from them. It holds no `if`, `else`, `switch`, `match`, `when`, `guard` or ternary (`? :`). It holds no loop, no `&&`, `||`, `??`, `and` or `or`, and no `try` or `catch`. This includes the code of a lambda that the method writes. Kotlin's `?:` counts as a decision, except in the early exit below. Optional chaining such as `order?.total` and Rust's `?` operator are allowed. In Go, the error check that does the job of Rust's `?` is allowed too: `if err != nil { return ..., err }` right after the statement that sets `err`, with one `return` in its body whose last value is `err` or `fmt.Errorf("...: %w", err)`, and no `else`. Any other statement in that body, an `else`, or a second condition makes it a decision again. Swift's `guard let x = <expression> else { return nil }` and Kotlin's `val x = <expression> ?: return null` are allowed for the same reason: one binding, no `,`, `&&` or `||` in the condition, and only a `return` of nothing or of one name, literal or number. A `guard` with a test, a second binding or another statement, and an `?:` with a default value, still count.

A private method holds at most one decision or one loop. An `else if` chain is one decision, and an `&&` or `||` inside its condition is part of that decision. A private method that makes a decision does not call another private method that also makes a decision. A call such as `items.map(item => item.id)` is not a loop, because its lambda holds no decision. `items.filter(item => item.ready && item.shown)` is a loop. In a Go iterator, the stop check `if !yield(item) { return }` is not a decision: it is part of `yield`, which stops by itself in the other languages.

The build refuses a service or a controller that breaks these rules with `TY1314`. The message names the method and the construct, and it shows how to write a private method in that language. `ty migrate check` lists every place to change.

| Language | Private method |
| --- | --- |
| JavaScript | A name that starts with `_`, such as `_pick(items)` |
| TypeScript | `private pick(items)` |
| Python | A name that starts with `_`, such as `def _pick(self, items)` |
| Ruby | A method below `private` |
| PHP, Java, Kotlin, C# | A method with the `private` keyword |
| Swift | A method with `private` or `fileprivate` |
| Dart | A name that starts with `_` |
| Go | A method with a lowercase name |
| Rust | A method without `pub`. The methods of `impl Trait for Type` are public. |

In every language, a method whose name starts with `_` is private.

This check is new, so you can turn it off for one side of the app while you move code. For Tac services, set `tac.cohesion.check` to `false` in `client/manifest.json`. For Yon services and controllers, set `cohesion.check` to `false` in `server/application.json`. Use these settings only for migration.
